---
title: "Attackability"
---

Every conjecture under `c/` has a score out of 31, answering one question: **if a machine had a fixed
budget and attacked this, would it come back with something correct, not trivial, and not already
known?** Higher is better.

It is not how likely the statement is to be true, not how hard it is for a person, and not how
important it is.

## Not the difficulty grade

The [difficulty grade](/reviews/status-badge/index.qmd#difficulty-legend) measures how far a statement
is from known technique. This measures effort, for one worker: a machine on a budget.

They disagree often. [c/0001](/c/0001/) scores 11, because a person knows what to try but the answer is
a simulator, with no number to compute and no small case to check. [c/0015](/c/0015/) scores 25, because
nobody has ever attempted it and you can check the answer by brute force on ten leaves.

So this is not a ranking of importance. Eight of the top nine were raised in one sentence by their own
source and dropped.

## What the score is made of

**Can it find anything? (12)** Machines build things well and prove non-existence badly. Asking for a
construction scores well; asking for a lower bound against unlimited preprocessing scores near zero.

**Can you tell if the answer is right? (12)** Same weight, on purpose. The usual failure is not a wrong
proof but a **correct proof of a slightly different statement**, which passes every local check.

**Has anyone tried, and can you get the papers? (7)** A conjecture mentioned once and dropped beats a
famous one.

**Penalties** come off mainly for the answer possibly being in the training data already, where recall
looks like discovery.

| The eight questions | Out of |
|---|---|
| Build something, or rule something out? | 4 |
| Is there a settled special case to climb from? | 4 |
| How many papers must be combined? | 4 |
| **Is the statement pinned to exactly one reading?** | **6** |
| Is there a small case you can settle exactly? | 3 |
| Can a proof assistant hold it? | 3 |
| Did anyone ever try? | 4 |
| Are the sources reachable, and the proof short? | 3 |

Two are counterintuitive. **Long and boring beats short and clever**: needing a whole new idea caps
that question at 1. And **obscurity counts in favour**, because being open usually means nobody looked.

## Bands and verdicts

The band is the same number read as difficulty, for this machine rather than in general.

| Band | Score | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `prime` | 26 to 31 | Start here. |
| `reachable` | 22 to 25 | Worth a full attempt. |
| `stretch` | 18 to 21 | Search the literature, try to refute it, plan the special cases. No proof budget yet. |
| `hard` | 15 to 17 | Same, and expect the refutation attempt to be the whole return. |
| `very hard` | 8 to 14 | Expect a note saying why it is stuck. |
| `out of reach` | 0 to 7 | No proof budget. |
| `gated` | n/a | Stopped before scoring. |

`go` needs 22, with at least 7 in each of the first two groups; `probe` needs 15; below that is `park`.
A statement whose reading cannot be pinned is capped at `probe`. One that is cheap to try to refute is
promoted from `park` to `probe`, which is why [c/0050](/c/0050/), [c/0051](/c/0051/) and
[c/0053](/c/0053/) are probes at 11, 12 and 14.

## The ranking

Scored 23 August 2026, and the corpus has moved since. Two things to know before using the table.

**One entry is out of date.** [c/0048](/c/0048/) is marked `go` below but has since been **solved**,
affirmatively and more strongly than the conjecture asked: a signed reweighting reaching an exact
rank-one second moment at entropy cost O(log n), below every n^delta. Its row is kept, struck through,
rather than deleted, so the scale can still be judged against a case whose answer is now known.

**Ten conjectures are missing.** This scored 55 statements; there are now 65. [c/0057](/c/0057/)
through [c/0066](/c/0066/) have never been scored and do not appear.

Beyond those, check a conjecture's own page before starting: work can be in flight that this snapshot
does not know about. [c/0010](/c/0010/) is top of the table and already has a partial solution, now
blind-verified.

## What the pass found

**Fourteen were stopped before scoring.** A stop is not a bad grade.

- **Two need another famous problem solved first.** Proving [c/0011](/c/0011/) would give P ≠ NP;
  [c/0056](/c/0056/) is stopped by a theorem in its own source. Disproving either is cheap and not
  blocked.
- **Five need their statement fixed:** [c/0016](/c/0016/), [c/0019](/c/0019/), [c/0039](/c/0039/),
  [c/0040](/c/0040/) and [c/0003](/c/0003/) all rest on something their source never pins down.
- **Seven are already solved.** Six confirm the site's own August sweep; [c/0004](/c/0004/) has an
  unreviewed proof here, so what is left is checking.

**[c/0003](/c/0003/) is false as written, and should be fixed first.** There is no salt, so the offline
stage can store one k-collision and the online stage print it without a single query, breaking the
claimed tradeoff outright. Everything the page cites assumes a salt drawn *after* the advice is fixed.

**[c/0024](/c/0024/) is out of date.** A CRYPTO 2024 follow-up reaches `N^1.6` in Maurer's model under
a strong assumption. That does not settle the page, whose statement allows none, but the page does not
record it.

**Four pairs are near-twins that can answer each other's question.** [c/0008](/c/0008/) and
[c/0009](/c/0009/) share identical LaTeX stating two different conjectures, as do [c/0004](/c/0004/)
and [c/0005](/c/0005/); [c/0050](/c/0050/) and [c/0053](/c/0053/) differ by one word; and
[c/0024](/c/0024/) and [c/0025](/c/0025/) differ by which group model.

**Most of this corpus asks you to build something:** 27 constructions against 20 lower bounds.
[c/0051](/c/0051/) scores 12, while [c/0052](/c/0052/), asking for the attack that would refute it,
scores 24. Every lower-bound record names the thing you would build to disprove it, and that is usually
the part worth attacking.

## How much to trust this

One machine, one pass. The totals, verdicts and bands are computed from the eight numbers and the set
passes its validator, so the arithmetic is checkable; the eight numbers themselves are opinions with a
written reason attached. Re-checking them in the same sitting moved four by a point each, so a fresh
pass would move more. Where evidence is thin, grades round towards *harder than it looks*.

## Provenance

Produced by the `conjecture-triage` skill on 23 August 2026 over all 55 conjectures under `c/`;
[c/0005](/c/0005/) is left out, having been withdrawn. The other 54 records carry the reason behind
each number, the literature search, the thing you would build to disprove each statement, and a
suggested first step: see
[the audit record](https://github.com/crypto-conjura/crypto-conjura.github.io/blob/main/audits/2026-08-23-conjecture-attackability-triage.md)
and its
[machine-readable companion](https://github.com/crypto-conjura/crypto-conjura.github.io/blob/main/audits/2026-08-23-conjecture-attackability-triage.records.jsonl),
which label the eight questions `P1` `P2` `P3`, `V1` `V2` `V3`, `O1` `O2`.

A dated snapshot, not a live view: attackability is deliberately not yet a field on each conjecture.
